item.title: EU Parliament committee nears deal on EU‑US trade pact
item.description: “We must set clear boundaries and be ready to freeze negotiations or the application," said S&D trade committee chair Bernd Lange

item.title: Out of the cold: Growing number of EU capitals seek talks with Russia
item.description: The move would de facto end Russian president Vladimir Putin's diplomatic isolation by the West over his full invasion of Ukraine.

item.title: Revealed: How Big Tech is lobbying on forthcoming EU Digital Fairness Act
item.description: New research by the Brussels NGO Corporate Europe Observatory (CEO) details an intense lobbying campaign by Big Tech to weaken the upcoming EU Digital Fairness Act — a proposal that aims to protect consumers from deceptive or addictive online features.

item.title: The latest Greek tragedy — what the law actually says about maritime intercepts
item.description: This week's fatal collision between a Greek coast guard vessel and a migrant boat off the island of Chios has once again brought European maritime enforcement practices under scrutiny, raising questions about accountability and balance between border control and the protection of human life at sea.

item.title: Listen: How did radical far-right parties become central to Europe’s political scene?
item.description: From Italy to Poland, Europe’s far right keeps radicalising. New extremist parties, shifting norms, social media and democratic fatigue—how did the unthinkable become mainstream politics across the continent today now?

item.title: 66 days to election: Dangerous moment for Orbán’s Fidesz as conflict with Roma voters escalates
item.description: In this week's round-up from the Hungarian election campaign: Viktor Orban's name in the Epstein files, more fallout from the Roma remarks, and all the latest opinion polling.

item.title: Shared China dilemma pushes EU and US into new minerals pact
item.description: The promise of an EU-US deal on critical minerals is one of the most significant cases of a transatlantic trade alliance since the start of Donald Trump’s second presidential term. What could this mean for Europe and supply chains?

item.title: EU Commission sued over lithium push in landmark raw materials case
item.description: The European Commission is being sued for the first time for granting a lithium mine in Portugal so-called "strategic project" status under the bloc's Critical Raw Materials Act, allegedly without pursuing sufficient environmental assessments.

item.title: Covid fund transparency gap risks EU court battle, warns lead MEP
item.description: Financial watchdogs sitting in the European Parliament have cast serious doubt on the integrity of the EU's Covid recovery fund — and threatened court action over its lack of transparency.

item.title: Grok scandal prompts MEP move to ban non-consensual AI porn in new omnibus
item.description: A new draft report by Green MEP Sergey Lagodinsky aims to amend the AI Omnibus proposal to prohibit generative apps that can generate nonconsensual sensualised content.
